title: If it rains, we’ll…
goal: Agree on a realistic backup plan for a day out
freeConversationInstruction: What shall we do if it rains this weekend? Plan something you’d enjoy in either kind of weather

pages.title: Review the last lesson
pages.instruction: Pick a hotel for our trip and explain your choice

items.prompt: For our trip, would you prefer a hotel near the centre or one by the beach?
items.hint: I’d choose the one by the beach
items.cue: Choose one of the two hotels

items.prompt: What makes it a better option for you?
items.hint: It’s quieter / The other one is closer to the shops

items.prompt: What would make a hotel a bad choice for you?
items.hint: It’s too far from the centre / The rooms aren’t big enough
items.cue: Give one reason you’d choose another hotel

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Shall we go on a hike on Sunday?
lines.audioText: Shall we go on a hike on Sunday?
lines.translation: Vamos fazer uma caminhada no domingo?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: I’d like that. What does the forecast say?
lines.audioText: I’d like that. What does the forecast say?
lines.translation: Eu gostaria. O que diz a previsão?

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: It might rain. If it rains, we’ll go to the museum instead
lines.audioText: It might rain. If it rains, we’ll go to the museum instead.
lines.translation: Pode chover. Se chover, vamos ao museu

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Good plan. What time is the bus?
lines.audioText: Good plan. What time is the bus?
lines.translation: Bom plano. Que horas é o ônibus?

questions.prompt: What is their first plan for Sunday?
questions.answer: Their first plan is to go on a hike

questions.prompt: What will they do if it rains?
questions.answer: If it rains, they’ll go to the museum instead

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: At nine. If we miss it, we can take the next one at nine thirty
lines.audioText: At nine. If we miss it, we can take the next one at nine thirty.
lines.translation: Às nove. Se perdermos, podemos pegar o próximo às nove e meia

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: All right. I’ll bring a raincoat. What about lunch?
lines.audioText: All right. I’ll bring a raincoat. What about lunch?
lines.translation: Tudo bem. Vou levar uma capa de chuva. E o almoço?

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: If we go to the museum, we’ll eat at the café inside

lines.translation: Se formos ao museu, vamos comer no café lá dentro

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Great. Let’s check the weather again before we leave
lines.audioText: Great. Let’s check the weather again before we leave.
lines.translation: Ótimo. Vamos conferir o tempo de novo antes de sair

questions.prompt: What will they do if they miss the nine o’clock bus?
questions.answer: They can take the next bus at nine thirty

questions.prompt: Where will they eat if they go to the museum?
questions.answer: They’ll eat at the café inside the museum

pages.title: Make a backup plan
pages.instruction: We’re taking the bus to go hiking. Make a plan in case the weather or transport changes

items.prompt: What will you do if it rains?
items.cue: Suggest a realistic alternative for the outing

items.prompt: What if the bus is late?
items.cue: Agree on a second way to reach the destination
items.hint: If the bus is late, we can …

items.prompt: How will we keep each other updated?
items.cue: Agree on how to confirm or change the plan

pages.title: Build a first conditional sentence
pages.instruction: Talk about a real future possibility and the response you plan

rows.subject: Condition and result
rows.verb: If + present simple, will + base verb
rows.example: If it rains, we’ll go to the museum

rows.subject: Negative condition or result
rows.verb: If + don’t / doesn’t + base, will / won’t + base
rows.example: If the bus doesn’t come, we won’t wait outside

rows.subject: Ask about the result
rows.example: What will you do if it rains?

pages.note: Use present simple after if for this future condition. You can reverse the clauses: We’ll go to the museum if it rains. Use a comma when the if-clause comes first.

pages.title: Make a plan B
pages.instruction: Agree on Plan A and Plan B, including what you’ll do if something changes

pages.title: Listen and answer
pages.instruction: Use the backup plan. Listen to both voice notes, then answer and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana! The forecast says it will rain on Sunday morning. Let’s use our backup plan. If it rains, we’ll go straight to the museum, and we’ll have lunch inside
pages.audioText: Hi, Ana! The forecast says it will rain on Sunday morning. Let’s use our backup plan. If it rains, we’ll go straight to the museum, and we’ll have lunch inside.

items.prompt: Which plan does Priya suggest using?
items.answer: Priya suggests using the museum backup plan

items.prompt: What bus can they still take?
items.answer: They can still take the nine o’clock bus

items.prompt: What should they do if that bus is late?
items.answer: They should wait for the nine thirty bus rather than walk in the rain

additionalAudios.audioText: We can still take the nine o’clock bus. If that bus is late, let’s wait for the nine thirty one rather than walk in the rain. Does that work for you?
additionalAudios.message: We can still take the nine o’clock bus. If that bus is late, let’s wait for the nine thirty one rather than walk in the rain. Does that work for you?

pages.title: Respond to the message
pages.instruction: Confirm the weather and transport plan. Use the message to update your response and agree on the next step

items.prompt: Why does that option fit the traveller’s deadline?

items.prompt: What will you do if bad weather changes your day out?
items.hint: Use If and a practical alternative
items.answer: Example: If it rains, we’ll visit the museum instead
